Add your own detection to sipnab's diagnosis, without forking it.

A plugin is a small WebAssembly module. It receives one reconstructed dialog
and returns findings.

- Its findings appear in `--json-dialogs` output, in a `plugin_findings`
  array on the dialog they describe.
- The other surfaces (the report, REST, MCP, the TUI) do not show them yet.

## When you want one

sipnab already lets you *select* dialogs:

- the [filter DSL](@/docs/filter-dsl.md) picks them by field,
- [NDJSON](@/docs/output-formats.md) pipes them anywhere,
- `--alert exec` reacts to them.

What none of those do is *diagnose*:

- express a site-specific fault pattern,
- and have sipnab report it as a finding, with evidence, on the dialog it
  describes. Today that is the `--json-dialogs` output only; see
  [Known limits](#known-limits).

That is the one hole a plugin fills.

- If you can already answer your question with a filter or a `jq` pipeline,
  use those.
- They need no build step and no trust decision.

## What it costs you to trust one

A plugin is a `.wasm` file. That is exactly the kind of artifact people copy
off the internet. So read this before loading one someone sent you.

**A plugin has no imports at all.** Not a restricted set — none.

- No WASI, no filesystem, no network, no clock, not even logging.
- The only things crossing the boundary are:
  - integers,
  - the bytes sipnab copies into the plugin's own linear memory.
- A module that imports anything fails to instantiate.

| Bounded | How |
|---|---|
| CPU | Fuel metering. A plugin that loops forever gets cut off and reported as a plugin error, and the capture continues |
| Memory at run time | 16 MiB linear-memory ceiling, refused by the engine at the point of growth |
| Memory at load time | sipnab reads the `.wasm` file through a 16 MiB bound, so it never allocates a length the file chose |
| Output size | 4 MiB per reply |
| Blast radius | A trap, an exhausted fuel budget or a malformed reply fails *that dialog's* plugin findings, and nothing else |

**What is not bounded is what it reads.**

- A plugin sees every dialog sipnab reconstructs. This includes
  `Authorization` headers and `MESSAGE` bodies.
- It cannot send them anywhere. It has no imports.
- But it can decide what to report. A finding's `summary` is a string it chose.
- Load a plugin the way you would run a script:
  - from someone you trust,
  - or after reading it.

Plugins need a build with `--features plugins`. That feature is **not** in the
default feature set.

- A stock binary carries no interpreter at all. So `sipnab --version` tells
  you whether the machine in front of you can load one.
- These released builds include it:
  - the Linux gnu tarballs,
  - the `.deb` and `.rpm` packages,
  - the macOS builds.
- These do not:
  - the static musl tarballs,
  - the gnu `-noaudio` packages.

## Before you start

- **A sipnab with the `plugins` feature.** Every release package has it.
  `sipnab --version` lists `plugins` among the features. A source build needs
  `--features plugins` or `--features full`.
- **Rust with the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target,** to build a plugin:
  `rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
- **Nothing on any other system.** A plugin runs inside sipnab, on the
  dialogs sipnab already holds. It needs no SIP server, relay or network
  change.
- **Where findings appear.** Only `--json-dialogs` prints them, as
  [Known limits](#known-limits) says.

## Writing one, start to finish

The worked example is [`crates/sipnab-plugin-example`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/tree/main/crates/sipnab-plugin-example).
It flags **short answered calls**. These are calls picked up and torn down
inside five seconds. Such a call means one of:

- a bad route,
- a codec the far end rejected,
- wangiri-style fraud dialing.

It is deliberately not a built-in.

- Whether three seconds is a problem depends entirely on your traffic.
- That is the shape a plugin is for.

### A crate that builds to WASM

```toml
[lib]
crate-type = ["cdylib"]
```

Target `wasm32-unknown-unknown`. `std` works there.

- A `no_std` plugin is smaller.
- But it needs its own allocator and panic handler.
- That is a lot of ceremony for a detection.

### Three exports, and nothing imported

```rust
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn sipnab_plugin_abi_version() -> i32 { 1 }

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn sipnab_alloc(len: i32) -> i32 { /* host writes input here */ }

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn sipnab_analyze(ptr: i32, len: i32) -> i64 {
    // read UTF-8 JSON at (ptr, len), return (out_ptr << 32) | out_len
}
```

There is no deallocator. That is deliberate rather than an omission.

- sipnab instantiates the module once per dialog.
- It drops the store when `sipnab_analyze` returns.
- So the plugin's entire linear memory goes with it. There is nothing left to
  reclaim.
- Both documents used to require a `sipnab_dealloc` that the host never looked
  up.
  - So a plugin that omitted it loaded and ran anyway.
  - A requirement nothing checks teaches an author to distrust the rest of the
    page.

sipnab checks the ABI version at load rather than on first use.

- A plugin built against a later ABI would misread its input and report
  confident nonsense.
- That is worse than not loading.

### Read the input, return findings

Look at the input before writing code. It is the same per-dialog JSON
`--json-dialogs` emits, with the `messages` array alongside it:

```sh
sipnab -N -I capture.pcap --json-dialogs --no-cli-print | head -1
```

Return findings in this shape:

```json
{ "findings": [ { "id": "short-answered-call",
                  "summary": "Call answered and torn down after 2.2s (under 5s) — check routing, codec negotiation, or dial fraud.",
                  "evidence": [3, 5] } ] }
```

`evidence` indexes the dialog's own message list. It is **mandatory**.

- sipnab rejects a finding that leaves it empty.
- Every built-in detection names the messages behind it.
- A third-party finding answers to the same rule rather than entering as a
  lesser citizen.

### Build and run it

```sh
# Run all of these, in order.
rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown
cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p sipnab-plugin-example

sipnab -N -I capture.pcap --json-dialogs --no-cli-print \
  --plugin target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/sipnab_plugin_example.wasm
```

`--plugin` is repeatable.

- Each plugin gets its own sandbox.
- A failure in one never stops the capture or the others.

**What it printed.** On 2026-11-03, sipnab 0.5.232 read
[`tests/pcap-samples/sip-proxy.pcap`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/raw/main/tests/pcap-samples/sip-proxy.pcap) with the example plugin. The call there
ends 2.2 seconds after its answer, so the plugin reported it:

```sh
sipnab -N -I tests/pcap-samples/sip-proxy.pcap --json-dialogs --no-cli-print \
  --plugin target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/sipnab_plugin_example.wasm \
  | jq -c 'select(.plugin_findings != null) | {call_id, plugin_findings}'
```

```json
{"call_id":"proxied-call-synth@192.0.2.101","plugin_findings":[{"evidence":[6,9],"id":"short-answered-call","plugin":"sipnab_plugin_example","summary":"Call answered and torn down after 2.2s (under 5s) — check routing, codec negotiation, or dial fraud."}]}
```

A call the plugin reports nothing for carries no `plugin_findings` key.

### When it does not work

A plugin that does not load does not stop the run. sipnab logs the reason,
reads the capture without that plugin, and exits `1`. Every report the run
prints says so, for example `--report`:

```text
INCOMPLETE RUN — this report does not describe the whole capture:
  - 1 of 1 requested --plugin(s) did not load; findings they would have contributed are absent
```

| sipnab logs | Cause and fix |
|---|---|
| `plugin <path>: cannot read plugin: <path>: No such file or directory (os error 2)` | The path is wrong. `cargo build` writes the module under `target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/`. |
| `plugin <path>: not a valid WASM module:`, then the parser's report | The file is not a WebAssembly module. Build with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, and pass the `.wasm` file. |
| `Error: unexpected argument '--plugin' found`, and exit `2` | The build left out the `plugins` feature, so the binary has no `--plugin` flag. `sipnab --version` lists the features. Every release package has `plugins`, through `full`. A source build needs `--features plugins` or `--features full`. |

A plugin that loads and then fails on one dialog drops only its findings for
that dialog, and the run goes on: see `plugin {} on {}: {e}` in
[Error messages](@/docs/errors.md).

### Where the findings come out

Under a top-level `plugin_findings` array, separate from `signaling_diagnosis`.

- Each finding carries the plugin's own name.
- sipnab fills in that name from the file stem, never the plugin.
- So a plugin cannot attribute a finding to another plugin or to a built-in
  detection.

That separation is the point. A reader can always tell which findings sipnab
stands behind and which came from third-party code.

Against
[`tests/pcap-samples/sip-over-tcp.pcap`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/raw/main/tests/pcap-samples/sip-over-tcp.pcap),
a call answered and hung up 2.2 seconds later, the example plugin reports:

```bash
sipnab -N -I tests/pcap-samples/sip-over-tcp.pcap --json-dialogs --no-cli-print --quiet --plugin target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/sipnab_plugin_example.wasm | jq -c 'select(.plugin_findings != null) | {call_id, plugin_findings}'
```

```json
{"call_id":"over-tcp-synth@198.51.100.100","plugin_findings":[{"evidence":[3,5],"id":"short-answered-call","plugin":"sipnab_plugin_example","summary":"Call answered and torn down after 2.2s (under 5s) — check routing, codec negotiation, or dial fraud."}]}
```

A dialog the plugin has nothing to say about carries no `plugin_findings`.

## When a plugin does not load

sipnab still reads the capture and prints every dialog, without the findings
that plugin would have added. It logs the reason, and the run exits 1. The
last line of `--json-dialogs` says so as well:

```json
{"sipnab_run":{"archives":{"cut_short":false},"files":{"given":1,"not_reached":0,"read_in_full":1,"skipped":0,"stopped_early":0},"input_complete":false,"plugins":{"failed":1,"loaded":0,"requested":1},"port_gate":{"sip_outside_portrange":0,"sip_outside_ws_ports":0},"reasons":["1 of 1 requested --plugin(s) did not load; findings they would have contributed are absent"],"retention":{"messages_dropped":0}}}
```

| Logged reason | Cause | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `plugin <path>: cannot read plugin: <path>: No such file or directory` | The path is wrong | Give the path to the `.wasm` file |
| `plugin <path>: not a valid WASM module` | The file is not WebAssembly, or a build for another target | Build for `wasm32-unknown-unknown` |
| An ABI version refusal | Someone built the plugin against another plugin ABI version | Rebuild it against the ABI this sipnab reports |
| `plugin <name> on <Call-ID>: <reason>` | The plugin loaded, then trapped, ran out of fuel or memory, or returned the wrong shape for one dialog | That dialog prints without the plugin's findings, and the other dialogs keep theirs. Fix the plugin |
| sipnab refuses the command line, exit 2, at `--plugin` | A build without the `plugins` feature has no `--plugin` flag | Use a build that lists `plugins` in `sipnab --version` |

[Error messages](@/docs/errors.md) explains each message in full.

## Known limits

- Findings reach `--json-dialogs` only. The report, REST, MCP and the TUI do
  not show them.
- One hook point: post-dialog analysis.
  - There is deliberately no packet-level hook.
  - Handing every packet to an interpreter would undo the capture path's
    performance, and the [benchmarks](@/docs/benchmarks.md) with it.
- Plugins observe rather than mutate.
  - A plugin that could rewrite a dialog would make every other surface's
    output unattributable.
